text.p: Following are the main stories in Thursday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- State investment arm Khazanah Holdings Bhd is studying a proposal to participate in the rescue of bankrupt Dutch aircraft maker Fokker, said Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad.
-- Utility firm Tenaga Nasional Bhd plans to hive off its power generation unit which may eventually be listed on the Kuala Lumpur bourse, said its executive chairman Ahmad Tajuddin Ali.

-- A Russian company will be engaged to launch Malaysia's first micro-satellite at the end of the year, said Science, Technology and Environment Minister Law Hieng Ding. He did not identify the company.

-- About 2,000 drug addicts will be returned to their families after being treated with naltrexone pills, a drug to supress their addiction to heroin and morphine in a pilot scheme to be launched next month, said Deputy Home Minister Megat Junid Megat Ayub.
-- Police have arested 24 students suspected to be marijuana addicts and pushers from a secondary school in southern Johor state.
